title: 3D Gaussian Splatting within Self-Learned Neural View-Dependent Color Fields
claim: Per-point positions query multi-resolution feature grids, an MLP predicts view-dependent colors, and self-supervision plus Lipschitz regularization constrain the color field.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right flow, braces labeling stages, curved skip arrows
description: A single wide left-to-right diagram. At far left, colored dots labeled 'Gaussian Centers' feed a red query point, shown as a long arrow. The arrow passes through two hexagonal multi-resolution grids labeled Level 1 and Level N, with an ellipsis between them. Curved arrows carry features from the grids into a stacked column of colored feature cells (blue, orange, purple). A 'Ray' arrow also enters this column. The column feeds a small neural network drawing labeled MLP, topped with a 'Lipschitz Regularization' brace. The MLP outputs an RGB column of red, green and blue cells. The RGB column splits two ways. One branch goes to a '3DGS Rasterizer' box, together with an 'Attributes' box, and produces an Image. The other goes to a 'Self-Supervision' cluster of dots labeled No Color and Surface Color. Braces underneath label Slicing, Features and MLP. Black lines on a white background with small colored accents.
caption: Overview of our framework. We first use Gaussian centers to query multi-resolution feature grids to obtain features. Then, together with view directions, we employ an MLP to predict view-dependent colors for each Gaussian. The predicted colors and Gaussian attributes are then rendered by the differentiable rasterizer. We impose self-learned supervision on the neural color field.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a vital tool in novel view synthesis. 3D Gaussian functions with attributes like color, opacity, and scale are stacked together to explicitly model a radiance field. However, discrete 3D Gaussians usually produce poor depth with few geometry details but lots of floaters, which hinders the effective modeling of smooth radiance fields. To address this issue, we propose to learn a radiance field within a continuous view-dependent color field parameterized by neural networks. With continuous constraints in color, the bias on low-frequency signals of neural networks can highly encourage the geometry modeling to contribute to high-frequency color variations on images, getting rid of solely relying on the color attribute itself. Moreover, we impose a constraint to improve the Lipschitz continuity of the neural color field, making large changes of each Gaussian's color also match with large changes of its position in terms of a ratio. To this end, we additionally introduce novel self-learning strategies to improve the learning of the neural view-dependent color field without any external knowledge or priors, aiming for better generalization on unseen scenes. Our numerical and visual comparisons on widely used benchmarks justify our idea and show better ability of high fidelity geometry recovery in 3DGS. Project page: https://github.com/yangyixi21/Neural-Color-Fields-3DGS.
